narrative: Three philosophers triangulate the mind-body problem from different angles: Ryle diagnoses the ghost-in-the-machine as a category mistake, Koestler argues that expelling the ghost discarded something real — genuine interiority at every level of a holon hierarchy — and Whitehead dissolves the problem entirely by treating experience as the interior dimension of all events rather than a product of biology. Together they move from diagnosis through loss to dissolution of the hard problem of consciousness.
